# Library semantics are data the analysis derives from decompiled code

Phase 5a described libraries in a table of C# families, one hand-written entry per overload, chosen
by a census of the calls the demo and the corpora make. It could not keep up with the ecosystem, and
it could not say the thing that mattered most. On eShop, 132 of the 142 semantic gaps after phase 5b
are calls that take a delegate: LINQ with lambdas, host and options callbacks, protobuf parsers,
Polly policies. A **Known call** never ran the user's code, so no entry could describe any of them.
What a library does with a caller's delegate is a question about executions — does it run the
delegate now, when a sequence is enumerated, when a member of some object is called, while the host
starts, or somewhere the analysis cannot see — and the engine already models every one of those.

The decision is that library semantics are data, and that most of the data is computed rather than
written:

- A **Library model** describes one member of one assembly version: what it does to each argument
  (none, **Deep read**, write), what it returns, and, for each delegate it receives, its **Delegate
  fate** — one of the executions the engine already has — with what each of the delegate's
  parameters is handed. What a call returns and what a delegate is handed are written in one small
  recursive language of values: an argument, what a delegate returned, the elements of a value, and
  a new **Library sequence**, grouping, collection or dictionary built from values. So `Where` returns
  a sequence of its source's elements, `Select` one of what its selector returned, `ToDictionary` a
  dictionary keyed by what one delegate returned and holding what the other returned, and each
  delegate is handed the elements of the source. A result the model does not describe is linked to
  nothing, as a known call's result was before. `di-factory` needs the service and the lifetime of a
  registration, so it comes with the generator, which derives it from a registration it sees. Models
  come in **Model layers** with provenance: built-in
  (shipped in the executable), project (written by the team in the repository), generated (by the
  **Model generator**) and AI. A project entry overrides every other layer, including by declaring
  a member opaque. Hand-written entries may name overloads by pattern; a lock file pins the exact
  declaration ids, so resolution stays by exact symbol and version (TD-122).
- The **Model generator** decompiles the library with ICSharpCode.Decompiler, which ships inside the
  executable as Z3 does (ADR 0004). The decompiled code goes through the analysis's own Roslyn
  frontend: there is no second frontend for libraries. For each member it writes a **Driver** — a
  small program whose action calls the member with probe lambdas — and reads where each probe's
  write lands: at the call, on enumeration of the result, or at a call of a member of the object
  that keeps the delegate. Drivers are synthesized from the member's signature; nobody writes them.
- Generated and project models live in the target repository, under `.concurrency-hunter/models/`
  next to the suppressions file, and are meant to be committed: a team reviews them, shares them and
  promotes a generated entry to a project entry by editing it. Built-in models cover popular
  packages and are generated by us before a release; the run generates only what is missing, for
  the members it actually reached, within a budget. One hand-written family covers a whole type
  rather than a census: every operator of `System.Linq.Enumerable` that takes a delegate and no
  comparer. They are the most frequent delegate gap, their semantics are documented operator by
  operator, and the generator reads them badly until the engine prunes type tests and reaches a
  library iterator's `MoveNext` (questions 38 and 39).
- The **Open-world rule** governs everything the generator concludes. Library code is not a closed
  world: whoever calls a stored delegate may be framework code no root reaches. A delegate the
  driver did not see run, or saw run and still kept after the call, runs in an **Unknown
  execution**. A delegate is `invoke-now` only when it ran during the call and nothing keeps it
  afterwards, which the heap decides, not the probe. A **Holder** is defined by reachability: a
  delegate reachable only through the object that keeps it runs wherever any member of that object
  runs; the triggers the driver happened to observe are information, never the whole list.
- AI models answer what neither the code nor the driver shows — mostly when a callback runs relative
  to startup and requests, and how often a DI factory runs. Only a model class shown to be
  calibrated on the gold set may produce them. A model from a non-manual layer may remove pairs the
  **Unknown effect** of that call would have made; coverage counts, per layer, the pairs each layer
  removed.

The research behind this measured each step on the 49 members behind eShop's delegate gaps, labelled
by hand and verified against the libraries' sources. Decompiled code compiles under Roslyn with
99.6–100% of method bodies free of errors, EF Core included. The engine on decompiled Polly placed a
retry callback in the request that executes the policy and found the `Task.Run` inside a
pessimistic timeout — semantics that depend on how the policy was configured, which no table can
express. Drivers synthesized from signatures compiled for all 131 members sampled from protobuf,
`System.Security.Claims`, Polly and LINQ, and their definite labels agreed with an independent
reading of the decompiled code on 125 of 131.

Rejected: hand-written families, the phase 5a format. They do not scale and they cannot describe
delegates without a vocabulary that is itself execution semantics. Rejected: an IL frontend of our
own. It is a second frontend to keep equivalent with the first, and it must rebuild what the
decompiler already reconstructs — lambdas, closures, `async` state machines — before it can answer
the one question it is good at, which is where a delegate goes. Rejected: analysing library bodies
as source inside every run. One Polly call grew the reachable bodies from 7 to about 150, and a
stored delegate that only the framework invokes silently stopped running: the protobuf parser
factory lost its finding with no gap and no counter. Rejected: models written by AI from the
signature and documentation alone. A calibrated model came close on famous packages, where it has
read the code, and a weaker one labelled retry callbacks `invoke-now` with confidence 0.85; the
code, not the documentation, has to be the input. Rejected: trusting the triggers a driver
observed. For a circuit breaker the driver saw `Isolate` break the circuit and missed `Execute`,
which breaks it on a failure; a model built on that list would have lost every race between the
callback and the requests that run the policy. Rejected: a single effect, `returns-arg`, for what a
call returns, as question 29 first asked. It says that `Take` yields its source's elements, but not
that `Select` yields what its selector returned, what a `ToDictionary` holds as keys and as values, or
what a `GroupBy` group holds. Rejected: handing each delegate parameter whatever of its type the
call's arguments reach. It needs no data, but it guesses at the library the model exists to
describe, and it cannot say where a delegate's result goes.

The consequences to hold. The plugin now writes to the repository, and only there: generated
models under `.concurrency-hunter/models/`, never a source file, project file or build output. The
cold performance targets are revised with generation in them. The engine's precision on library
code becomes product behaviour: a type test it does not prune or a factory-built receiver it loses
turns a precise model into an unknown execution, which is safe but costs findings. A decompiler bug
is silent when the result compiles; a member whose body does not compile is left opaque and
counted. A decompiled library runs through the same lowering as user code, so a defect the
generator hits there is a defect in user code too.
